The provided data from the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] offers a cross-sectional comparison of patient characteristics for those treated with [[bmsl|Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] across various Danish hospital departments [^src1]. Because this analysis is based on a single dated snapshot from 2025, it does not support claims regarding longitudinal trends or improvements over time; rather, it establishes a baseline of departmental volumes, diagnostic distributions, and demographic profiles [^src1].

In terms of overall patient volume, the leaders are Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg ([[ouh-svendborg|OUH Svendborg]]) with 1,338 patients, Aalborg Universitetshospital with 1,303 patients, [[sjellands-universitetshospital|Sjællands Universitetshospital]] with 1,257 patients, and [[amager-og-hvidovre-hospital|Amager og Hvidovre Hospital]] with 1,253 patients [^src1]. Conversely, the trailers in patient volume are Holbæk Sygehus with only 22 patients and Bornholms Hospital with 45 patients [^src1]. 

The diagnostic distribution highlights the widespread prevalence of [[dk50-crohns-sygdom|DK50* Crohns sygdom]] and [[dk51-ulceroes-colitis|DK51* Ulcerøs colitis]] across the network. However, specific departments act as outliers for rarer conditions. For instance, Regionshospitalet Horsens reports that 55% of its BMSL cohort (219 individuals) is treated for [[dk830f-primaer-skleroserende-kolangitis|DK830F Primær skleroserende kolangitis]], while Bornholms Hospital reports that 51% of its patients (23 individuals) are treated for [[dk912b-korttarmssyndrom|DK912B Korttarmssyndrom]] [^src1]. 

Demographically, the mean age (a_mean) of patients varies significantly by department. Nordsjællands Hospital and Holbæk Sygehus treat the oldest cohorts, with mean ages of 49 and 53 years, respectively [^src1]. In contrast, [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]] and Amager og Hvidovre Hospital treat the youngest cohorts, with mean ages of 36 and 35 years [^src1]. Gender distribution remains relatively balanced across the network, generally splitting near 50/50 between female (Kvinde) and male (Mand) patients [^src1]. Notably, Region Hovedstadens Psykiatri appears in the dataset but with suppressed figures (#) for total volumes and specific diagnoses, reporting only demographic metrics such as a mean age of 41 [^src1]. Similarly, [[rigshospitalet-med-klinik-mave-tarm-lever|Rigshospitalet Med. Klinik Mave-, Tarm- og Leversygd.]] has suppressed data for short bowel syndrome [[dk912b-korttarmssyndrom|DK912B Korttarmssyndrom]] [^src1].
